task: Decide and document the Koala CLI authority-client role before any enforce-mode implementation milestones begin.
outcome: User opens docs/requirements/decisions/authority-client-role.md and sees a clear PD-1 decision: whether Koala CLI is a thin local/shadow client or a first-class enforce-mode authority client, what L2+ evidence it may claim, and which Milestone 2-6 stories should run next.
facts: B-0f04 audit found FU-1/FU-2/FU-3 depend on PD-1 before implementation should start.
Current Koala CLI has authority POST plumbing but minimal unsigned EvidenceEnvelope submission and local lifecycle gates.
Cord Team Python authority can require production enforce handshake, signed actor payloads, run bindings, provider diversity, and server receipts.
Koala Mac/Swift runner already has actor-key registration, runner registration/heartbeat, and signed evidence submission paths.
INIT reviewers passed B-4bd4 but advised defining terms, durable decision location, and Milestone 2-6 routing explicitly.
constraints: This story is decision-only; no production TS/Python/Swift implementation changes.
Claude Code CLI performs decision artifact drafting; Codex acts as PM/verifier.
Do not imply L2+ authority guarantees from local JSON or natural-language conclusions.
Decision must be durable enough for future Koala CLI, Python authority, and Mac runner stories to reference.
High-risk story requires decision_set with at least three preMortem scenarios before DEV.
unknowns: Which PD-1 option will the evidence support as the recommended near-term choice.
Whether Koala CLI should ever submit L2+ evidence directly or only request/attach runner-generated receipts.
Which follow-up milestones become required, deferred, or documentation-only after PD-1 is chosen.
